_comment: The declared identity of the three scoring tables of openspec/specs/scoring/ §2,
and the release that last moved them.
SCR-2 makes those tables normative constants of the audit rather than
implementation details: a change to any value is a change of instrument, every
archived run scored under the previous table stops being comparable, and a trend
line spanning the change is a lie about the site.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO: it does not repeat the values. They are already
normative in §2 of the spec, and SCR-14's reader
(tests/test_runner.py::TheNormativeTablesAreReadFromTheDocument) holds the code
against that document row by row. A fourth transcription of the numbers here
would be exactly the hand-written set GOV-3 exists to count, and it would agree
with whichever copy was edited last.
What is left over after SCR-14 is the half of SCR-2 that is about people: that a
table change is *stated in the release that does it*. That needs one value SCR-14
has no use for — a name for the instrument as a whole, which a release note can
quote and a run artifact can carry. That is `stamp`.
To change a table: edit §2 of openspec/specs/scoring/spec.md and the constant in
scripts/checklist_runner.py together, run tests/test_scoring_tables.py to be told
the new stamp, put it here, move the old stamp to `supersedes`, set `declared_in`
to the release making the change, and write the marker line plus both stamps into
that release's CHANGELOG entry.
